originalTitle: South African white genocide does not exist, new ambassador to US tells BBC
title: Good News from South Africa: Everyone is Safe and Happy!
content:
Hello, my wonderful friends all across Africa! Your special news reporter is here with some very good news from a country called South Africa. It's a beautiful place right here on our amazing continent, filled with sunshine and lots of friendly people. Today, we're talking about a special helper from South Africa named Mr. Roelf Meyer. He is a very important person, and he had something really important to tell everyone. Let's find out what it was!

Meet Our Special Helper, Mr. Roelf Meyer

Mr. Roelf Meyer is a kind man from South Africa. He has white skin, just like some other people in South Africa. He knows his country very, very well because he lives there and loves it dearly. He wants everyone to know the truth about what is happening in South Africa. He has a very special job called an 'ambassador.' Did you know that an ambassador is like a super-duper messenger and friend for their country? They travel to other countries to talk to their leaders and tell them all about their home country. It helps countries be good friends and understand each other.

What is an Ambassador?

Imagine you want to tell your friend a secret, but your friend lives very far away. You might ask a trusted older brother or sister to carry your message carefully. An ambassador is a bit like that! Mr. Meyer is South Africa's special messenger to a far-away country called the United States of America. He helps them understand South Africa better. Did you know that every country has ambassadors? They work hard to make sure their country is understood and that everyone gets along. It's a bit like when you play with your friends, and you all want to be fair and kind to each other.

A Big Conversation About Fairness

So, what was the big message Mr. Meyer shared? Well, sometimes, people in other countries hear stories that might not be completely true. Some people were saying that white people in South Africa were being treated very, very badly, just because of their skin color. They thought white people were being hurt or made to leave their homes unfairly. This made many people around the world worried. But Mr. Meyer, who knows South Africa better than almost anyone, stepped up to tell everyone the real story. He talked to a big news place called the BBC, which is like a TV and radio station that tells people what's happening around the world.

Mr. Meyer Says: "That's Not True!"

Mr. Roelf Meyer looked at everyone and said, "No, that's not true! Everyone in South Africa is safe and cared for. There is no one being hurt or made to leave their homes just because they have white skin!" He said this with great confidence because he lives there! He sees with his own eyes. It's like if someone said your favourite toy was broken, but you know it's not, because you just played with it! He knows the truth because he is part of the community and experiences life in South Africa every day. Did you know it's really important to get information from someone who lives in the place they are talking about? They are the best people to tell us what is truly happening.

Why is it Important to Tell the Truth?

It's very, very important to tell the truth. When we tell the truth, everyone can feel safe and happy. If someone spreads a story that isn't true, it can make people scared or sad. Mr. Meyer bravely told the truth so that everyone could stop worrying and know that South Africa is a peaceful place for all its people. Talking truthfully helps countries be friends and helps people understand each other better. It stops worries and helps build trust, just like when you are honest with your friends, and they trust you even more.

South Africa: A Home for Everyone

South Africa is an amazing country often called the "Rainbow Nation." Did you know why? It's because lots of different people, with different skin colors, different languages, and different ways of living, all live there together! They are like the beautiful colors of a rainbow, all shining brightly together. Everyone is important, and everyone has a place. Mr. Meyer reminded the world that in South Africa, people work together to make sure everyone is treated fairly, no matter their skin color.

Let's Be Kind and Fair to All!

So, the good news is that South Africa is a safe and happy home for everyone who lives there. Mr. Roelf Meyer, our special ambassador, made sure to tell everyone the real story, spreading truth and peace. It's a wonderful reminder that we should always listen to people who know the truth and always be kind and fair to everyone, everywhere. That's all for today's good news from your friendly African news reporter! Remember to be kind, be truthful, and let's make our world a happier place, one good story at a time!
summary: A special helper from South Africa, Mr. Roelf Meyer, told people that everyone in his country, no matter their skin color, is safe and happy, correcting a worried story that wasn't true.
whyMatters: It's important because it helps everyone know the real truth about South Africa, so we can all be kind to each other and live in peace, like good friends who understand one another.

originalTitle: Are Ethiopians marching back to war in Tigray?
title: Let's Talk About Peace in Ethiopia!
content:
Hello from Ethiopia!

Hi everyone! Your friendly news reporter from Africa here! Today, we're going to talk about a very special country called Ethiopia. Ethiopia is a big and beautiful country in Africa, with amazing mountains, rivers, and lots of friendly people. It's a place where children like you go to school, play games, and laugh with their friends and families. **Did you know?** Ethiopia is one of the oldest countries in the whole world! It has a very long and interesting history, full of ancient stories and amazing places. Sometimes, even in the best places, grown-ups can have big disagreements. It's like when you and your friend argue about who gets to play with a toy, but much, much bigger. In Ethiopia, some grown-ups are having some big disagreements, and we want to understand it simply.

Who Lives in Ethiopia?

Ethiopia has many, many different groups of people. They speak different languages and have different traditions, but they all share the same beautiful country. Imagine your school with children from many different families; that's a bit like Ethiopia, but on a much larger scale! In Ethiopia, there are people who work for the whole country to keep everyone safe. We call them the "national army" or the "soldiers for the country." Their job is to protect everyone and make sure there is peace. There is also a group of people who are from a special part of Ethiopia called Tigray. Let's call them "the Tigray group." For a long time, these people were very important in helping to lead the country. They worked together with other leaders from different parts of Ethiopia. **Did you know?** Ethiopia is the birthplace of coffee! Yes, that yummy drink grown-ups love started its journey right there in Ethiopia. So next time your parents are drinking coffee, you can tell them it's from Ethiopia!

What is Happening Now?

Well, sometimes, grown-ups don't always agree on how things should be done in a country. The national army and the Tigray group have had some big disagreements. They didn't agree on who should lead, or how to share power, or how to make important decisions for everyone. These disagreements started to make everyone feel very worried and sad. It's like when friends stop talking to each other because they are upset. When people get very, very upset and don't talk, sometimes they start to fight. And fighting is never good.

Why Are People Worried?

A little while ago, sadly, there was some fighting in Ethiopia between the national army and the Tigray group. It made many people sad, and some families had to leave their homes to be safe. It was a very difficult time. But then, something good happened! Many, many people from other countries and good leaders worked very hard to help them stop fighting. They talked and talked, and finally, the fighting stopped. Everyone was very happy that the fighting was over. It was a big step towards peace. **Did you know?** Ethiopia has a special animal called the Gelada baboon! They are monkeys with bright red patches on their chests, and they are only found in Ethiopia! Now, even though the fighting stopped, the big disagreements about how to run the country are still there. It's like if you and your friend stopped yelling, but you still haven't agreed on who gets the toy. People are starting to feel worried again because the disagreements haven't gone away, and sometimes they seem to be getting worse. This is what we call "tension." Tension means people are feeling very upset and angry, and it makes everyone a bit nervous.

What is "Peace"?

Peace is a wonderful feeling. It means everyone is safe, happy, and not fighting. It means children can go to school without worrying, and families can live in their homes without fear. When there is peace, everyone can work together to make their country even better. **Did you know?** The capital city of Ethiopia is called Addis Ababa. It's a very busy and exciting city, full of markets, tall buildings, and friendly faces! Peace is like when you and your friend finally agree to share the toy, or take turns, and you can play happily together again. It's when everyone listens to each other and tries to understand.

How Can We Have Peace?

The most important way to have peace is to **talk**. Grown-ups, just like children, need to talk about their problems. They need to sit down, listen carefully to each other, and try to find ways to agree. It's like finding a solution where everyone feels a little bit happy, even if they don't get exactly what they want. They need to remember that everyone in Ethiopia is part of one big family, and families should always try to get along. Fighting only makes things worse and hurts everyone. Talking, sharing ideas, and being kind are the best ways to solve problems.

Friends Helping Friends

Many other countries and good people from around the world are trying to help Ethiopia. They are like kind teachers who help children resolve their arguments. They are encouraging the leaders of the national army and the leaders of the Tigray group to keep talking. They want to make sure that the disagreements don't lead to fighting again. They remind everyone how important it is for all the different groups in Ethiopia to work together. Because when everyone works together, amazing things can happen! **Did you know?** Ethiopia has many beautiful churches and monasteries carved right out of rocks! Some of them are thousands of years old and are truly amazing to see.

Our Big Hope for Ethiopia

So, even though there are still some worries, everyone hopes very much for peace in Ethiopia. We hope that the leaders will listen to each other, talk things through, and find a way for everyone to live happily and safely together. We hope that the children of Ethiopia will grow up in a country full of joy and friendship, where everyone helps each other. Just like you might learn to share your toys, or listen to your friends, the grown-ups in Ethiopia are learning how important it is to talk and work together. Let's all send our kind thoughts to Ethiopia and hope for a bright and peaceful future for all its wonderful people! **Did you know?** Ethiopia is home to part of the Great Rift Valley, a huge crack in the Earth's surface that stretches for thousands of kilometers across Africa! It's an incredible natural wonder.
summary: In Ethiopia, different groups are having disagreements, and everyone hopes they can talk to each other to find peace and avoid fighting again.
whyMatters: It's important because when people in a country don't get along, it can make everyone sad and unsafe, so we want them to talk and be friends so children can play and live happily.
